group_title: Television episodes from the Themed TV Episodes wiki hypnosis list (Nov 26)
description: Staging file for every missing episode on https://themed-tv-episodes.fandom.com/wiki/Episodes_about_Hypnosis (26 listed episodes, no subpages). Five episodes already in the catalog were not restaged (Adventures of Superman "The Secret of Superman" #2911; The Joseph Cotten Show "The Gentle Voice of Murder" #644; Surfside 6 "Power of Suggestion" #605; Temperatures Rising "Ellen's Flip Side" #3990; Columbo "A Deadly State of Mind" #1058/#3571/#1057). The 21 records here are episode-specific cards. Hypnosis plots were checked against at least one source besides the fandom page (Wikipedia, CTVA, Mental Block, show wikis, TV Guide, TVmaze, transcripts or reviews). Single-thin or conflicting-plot cases are tagged loose fit. Kids' and family shows are included as non-sexual entries and are not placed in adult or erotic categories. Pregnancy, kids together and prior kids are taken from the plot sources, with Unknown where the sources are silent. A whole-show catalog card was not treated as a duplicate unless it named the episode.

records.title: One Step Beyond — "Ordeal on Locust Street"
records.meta: TV anthology episode · USA · English · ABC · Season 2, Episode 2 · aired 22 Sep 1959
records.fit_note: Different episode from catalog card #3041 (One Step Beyond — "The Villa"). Adult daughter Anna is hypnotised only as a demonstration; the main treatment is of her brother Jason, a hidden, deformed young man whom a later review describes as older than a child. Non-sexual anthology story. The 'cure' of the deformity is presented as supernatural hypnosis/mind force.
records.character: Anna Parish (demonstration subject); her brother Jason Parish (the patient treated with 'mind force' hypnosis)
records.summary: The Parish family keeps their deformed, fish-like son Jason hidden in their Boston house. When Anna's fiancé Danny glimpses him and flees, Anna's mother refuses to send Jason to a hospital and instead calls in Dr. Edward Brown, a discredited doctor who uses a 'mind force.' He first hypnotises Anna as a demonstration (hand-raising, suggested burns, analgesia, a suggestion that she forget the pain of Danny leaving), then treats Jason. Three months later, on Christmas Eve, Jason appears as a handsome, unblemished young man. Host John Newland says Dr. Brown did not live to see hypnosis accepted by the medical community.
records.pregnancy_outcome: Not pregnant (no pregnancy in the cited plots)
records.pregnancy_note: Kids together: No. Anna is a young woman with a fiancé, not a mother in this episode.
records.kids_status: Has kids from before: No (Anna is the daughter in the household; no children of hers are mentioned)

records.title: The Flintstones — "Sleep On, Sweet Fred"
records.meta: Animated TV episode · USA · English · ABC · Season 4, Episode 10 (the fandom page wrongly lists it as Season 1, Episode 10) · aired 21 Nov 1963 · TV-G
records.fit_note: Family cartoon; non-sexual. This is sleep-teaching / sleep suggestion rather than a classic hypnotic induction; the Flintstones wiki notes the working title was 'Hypnotized Fred' and calls the TV doctor a hypnotist. Wilma and Betty are the ones giving the suggestions; Fred and Barney are the subjects. Series card #1235 does not name this episode. records.character: Fred Flintstone and Barney Rubble (sleep-taught by Wilma and Betty)
records.summary: Wilma and Betty watch a TV interview with Dr. Terratso Firma on mental conditioning and learn that repeating commands to a sleeping person can make him obey when he wakes. They whisper sleep suggestions to Fred and Barney (wipe their feet, ask for raises, prefer opera and shopping to bowling). It works until the men overhear the scheme and pretend they have been commanded to steal mink coats, luring the wives to a fur salon, where baby Pebbles throws a brick through the window and the two couples are arrested. The wives are punished for 'brainwashing' their husbands.
records.pregnancy_outcome: Not pregnant (Pebbles is already born; no new pregnancy in the plot). The hypnotised characters are the husbands.
records.pregnancy_note: Kids together: Yes — Fred and Wilma already have Pebbles (who appears in the episode). Betty and Barney have adopted Bamm-Bamm earlier in season 4, though he is not the focus here.

records.title: The Invaders — "Condition: Red"
records.meta: TV episode · USA · English · ABC · Season 2, Episode 1 · aired 5 Sep 1967 · science fiction
records.fit_note: The hypnotised person is Major Dan Keller (the husband), not his wife. Laurie is an Invader posing as his new wife and is the controller. The method is technological mind control (a red light from her ring plus a metal crown/head device), not a stage induction; theinvaders.tv and a later review describe it in those terms, and the fandom hypnosis list calls it hypnosis. Wikipedia describes him as being forced against his will to swap a NORAD tape but does not use the word hypnosis.
records.character: Major Dan Keller (Jason Evers), mind-controlled by his alien 'wife' Laurie Keller (Antoinette Bower)
records.summary: A doctor pronounces Laurie Keller dead after a riding fall, then is killed when she revives — she is a pulseless Invader. David Vincent investigates at NORAD, where her husband, Major Dan Keller, is a computer programmer. Laurie uses a red light from her ring and a metal head device to put Dan into a trance and make him swap a crucial NORAD tape so alien ships can approach Alaska undetected. Dan later confronts her, she is killed and disintegrates, and he dies after warning the base; NORAD switches to a backup program and the ships retreat. Dan had recently remarried after his first wife's death; the sources do not say whether that earlier death was the aliens' work.
records.pregnancy_outcome: Not applicable — the mind-controlled character is Dan, a man. Laurie is the controller, not a pregnant human wife.
records.pregnancy_note: Kids together: Unknown / not mentioned. Dan is a recent widower who has remarried Laurie.

records.summary: In the 'Rowdy Roddy Reforms' segment, Roddy Piper is hypnotised and starts acting uncharacteristically nice, to the confusion of Hulk Hogan and the alarm of the other heel wrestlers. The companion segment, 'Three Little Hulks,' has Hulk's three nephews visiting and causing trouble; it is not about hypnosis.
records.pregnancy_outcome: Not applicable — the hypnotised character is Roddy Piper, a man; no pregnancy plot.

records.title: My Secret Identity — "Trading Places"
records.meta: TV episode · Canada / USA · English · first-run syndication · Season 3, Episode 2 · aired 6 Oct 1990 (Wikipedia/TVmaze; the fandom page lists 8 Oct)
records.fit_note: Family/teen sitcom; non-sexual. The intended subject, Stephanie Clements (Wanda Cannon), is Andrew's adult mother, not a teenage girlfriend. Dr. Jeffcoate ('Dr. J') is the family's scientist neighbour, who is attracted to her but is not her husband. Andrew and Kirk (teenagers) are accidentally affected when the hypnotic light reflects off a window; they are not placed in an adult or sexual category. Series card #2390 is a whole-show card and does not name this episode.
records.character: Stephanie Clements (Andrew's mother), deliberately hypnotised by Dr. Benjamin Jeffcoate; Andrew Clements and Kirk Stevens are accidentally affected
records.summary: Dr. J uses a hypnotic device to make Stephanie, Andrew's mother, more impulsive. The hypnotic light reflects off a window, and Andrew and his friend Kirk are also put under; they fall into a hypnotic sleep and then start acting like one another.
records.pregnancy_outcome: Not pregnant (no pregnancy in the cited plots)
records.pregnancy_note: Kids together: No — Dr. J is the hypnotist and a neighbour, not Stephanie's partner in this plot, and no child with him is mentioned.
records.kids_status: Has kids from before: Yes (her son Andrew and daughter Erin)
